t: This was Toole's Theatre, a nineteenth-century West End building in William IV Street, near Charing Cross. Auditoria of various kinds stood on this site from 1832, used for religious and leisure activities. After rebuilding in 1881 and 1882, it held between 650 and 700 people. John Lawrence Toole owned it. He was an English comic actor and actor-manager, famous for farce, and the first actor to have a West End theatre named after him.
